+\small

+\toprule

+\midrule

+All three subcomponents independently achieve ${\geq}$99.50\% with 100\% fail recall (Table~\ref{tab:exc_subcomponent}), confirming that no single subcomponent is necessary for Tier~1 performance.
+\paragraph{Format marker confound.}

+\texttt{exc\_type\_only} and \texttt{exc\_stacktrace\_only} retain the \texttt{[ERROR]} prefix marker present in the full \texttt{exception\_only} format; \texttt{exc\_message\_only} contains only the bare exception class name and message text without any format markers.

+Because the marker alone is sufficient for near-perfect regex accuracy (B5: 99.33\%; \S\ref{sec:nomarker}), \texttt{exc\_type\_only} (100.00\%) and \texttt{exc\_stacktrace\_only} (99.83\%) are confounded with marker-based classification; we therefore do not make hierarchy claims among subcomponents.

+\texttt{exc\_message\_only} (99.50\%) provides a clean test: without any format markers, it achieves accuracy comparable to the full \texttt{exception\_only} condition (99.83\%), complementing the dedicated marker-removal ablation (\texttt{nomarker}: 97.65\%; \S\ref{sec:nomarker}) as additional evidence that the model learns semantic exception patterns rather than format shortcuts.

Tier~1 signals are individually sufficient: \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%$\pm$0.00) exceeds VOTA (99.05\%$\pm$0.38) by +0.78pp (2/3 seeds $p{<}.05$, all directionally consistent), implying that combining signals introduces noise.
Removing assertion points has no effect (\texttt{VOTA\_no\_ae} = 99.41\%, single seed), confirming exception dominance.
Individual exception subcomponents (type, stacktrace, message) each independently achieve ${\geq}$99.50\%, confirming that the binary presence of an exception event, rather than any specific subcomponent, drives Tier~1 performance (Appendix~\ref{sec:exc_subcomponent}).
The Tier~1/2 boundary is unambiguous: the lowest Tier~1 condition (\texttt{ae\_only} on DeepSeek, 98.53\%$\pm$0.30, 2 seeds) exceeds the highest Tier~2 (\texttt{loop\_only} on Qwen-7B, 86.05\%, CI [83.97, 87.96]) by 12.48\,pp with non-overlapping confidence intervals.
Gap statistic analysis independently supports $k{=}2$ clusters for 3/4 models and pooled data (silhouette ${\geq}$0.74).
Tier~2 \texttt{loop\_only} lifts over \texttt{no\_trace} are model-dependent: Qwen shows +10.92pp (7B) and +7.19pp (1.5B, $p{<}.0001$), with the larger 7B gain likely reflecting greater capacity to exploit structured loop patterns; DeepSeek +6.95pp (80.31\%), CodeLlama +0.93pp (77.40\%, n.s.).
\paragraph{Rule-based baseline comparison.}
The strongest non-trivial regex heuristic (B4: exception class name matching; Table~\ref{tab:regex}) achieves 93.61\% accuracy (F1=0.876), trailing SFT \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%, F1=0.997) by 6.22pp (McNemar $p{<}.001$).

lines: \paragraph{Diagnostic signal dilution in complete traces.}

1	\section{Introduction}
2	
3	Execution traces (line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior) have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models \citep{chen2025tracepile,ding2024traced,wang2025dcsh,ni2024next}.
4	The intuition is straightforward: more execution information should help the model make better predictions.
5	Yet for verdict prediction (classifying whether a test passes or fails), this intuition is wrong.
6	Complete traces \emph{actively degrade} accuracy compared to compact exception events, despite containing strictly more information.
7	
8	Prior work found trace utility to be task-dependent \citep{wang2025dcsh}, but focused on generation-oriented tasks where output noise confounds the analysis.
9	Verdict prediction offers a cleaner testbed: as binary classification, it isolates the learning signal from generation noise, and controlled component ablation directly measures how trace content affects SFT learning.
10	This approach aligns with recent *CL precedent: CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval} uses execution prediction to probe code reasoning, and NExT \citep{ni2024next} uses trace-augmented chain-of-thought for program repair.
11	
12	We present a systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction.
13	Using 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program}, we evaluate four models across three architecture families and 1.5B to 13B parameters: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B/1.5B-Instruct \citep{qwen2024coder}, CodeLlama-13B-Instruct \citep{roziere2024code}, and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct \citep{deepseek2024coder}.
14	
15	The central result: complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% across all models and seeds (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
16	A simple regex baseline (B5) that exploits the \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} format marker matches this ceiling at 99.33\%; even a trivial pattern suffices, so the interesting question is not why exceptions help but \emph{why complete traces hurt}.
17	Marker removal collapses B5 to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) confirms that SFT acquires language-level diagnostic patterns beyond format matching (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).
18	
19	A controlled gradient masking ablation limits gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\% of the degradation; content quality---diagnostic signal density at inference, the mechanism underlying what is intuitively termed ``information overload''---accounts for ${\geq}$95\% (\S\ref{sec:density}).
20	Training dynamics confirm this: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps, while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates between 82--89\% without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).
21	A tail-truncation budget sweep reveals a sharp performance jump at ${\sim}$512 tokens; this threshold coincides with the globals module dump (${\sim}$384 tokens), beyond which structured \texttt{[Line~X]} variable values appear (\S\ref{sec:trace_length}).
22	
23	Our contributions:
24	\begin{enumerate}
25	\item \textbf{Complete traces are strictly dominated by compact exception events}: across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}). Training dynamics directly show the mechanism: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).
26	
27	\item \textbf{SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns beyond format matching}: a regex exploiting format markers matches the exception ceiling (99.33\%), but marker removal collapses it to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) confirms the learned signal generalizes (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).
28	
29	\item \textbf{A two-tier signal hierarchy with a practical trace selection strategy}: Tier~1 (exceptions, assertions; ${\geq}$98.53\%) dominates Tier~2 (loop compression; 77--86\%) by 12+pp with non-overlapping CIs across all four models. A sharp performance transition at ${\sim}$512 tail tokens yields a practical fallback: exception events first, tail-truncated state otherwise (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, \S\ref{sec:trace_length}).
30	
31	\item \textbf{Controlled decomposition of the full-trace degradation}: gradient masking on \texttt{exception\_only} ($-$0.84pp under 99.8\% mask) limits gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\% of the 18pp gap; content quality (diagnostic signal density at inference) is the dominant factor at ${\geq}$95\%. A complementary label-only ablation on the Qwen family yields a directionally consistent but confounded upper bound (${\leq}$26\%) (\S\ref{sec:density}).
32	\end{enumerate}
33

\section{Introduction}

Execution traces (line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior) have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models \citep{chen2025tracepile,ding2024traced,wang2025dcsh,ni2024next}.
The intuition is straightforward: more execution information should help the model make better predictions.
Yet for verdict prediction (classifying whether a test passes or fails), this intuition is wrong.
Complete traces \emph{actively degrade} accuracy compared to compact exception events, despite containing strictly more information.

Prior work found trace utility to be task-dependent \citep{wang2025dcsh}, but focused on generation-oriented tasks where output noise confounds the analysis.
Verdict prediction offers a cleaner testbed: as binary classification, it isolates the learning signal from generation noise, and controlled component ablation directly measures how trace content affects SFT learning.
This approach aligns with recent *CL precedent: CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval} uses execution prediction to probe code reasoning, and NExT \citep{ni2024next} uses trace-augmented chain-of-thought for program repair.

We present a systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction.
Using 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program}, we evaluate four models across three architecture families and 1.5B to 13B parameters: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B/1.5B-Instruct \citep{qwen2024coder}, CodeLlama-13B-Instruct \citep{roziere2024code}, and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct \citep{deepseek2024coder}.

The central result: complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% across all models and seeds (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
A simple regex baseline (B5) that exploits the \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} format marker matches this ceiling at 99.33\%; even a trivial pattern suffices, so the interesting question is not why exceptions help but \emph{why complete traces hurt}.
Marker removal collapses B5 to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) confirms that SFT acquires language-level diagnostic patterns beyond format matching (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

A controlled gradient masking ablation limits gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\% of the degradation; content quality---diagnostic signal density at inference, the mechanism underlying what is intuitively termed ``information overload''---accounts for ${\geq}$95\% (\S\ref{sec:density}).
Training dynamics confirm this: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps, while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates between 82--89\% without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).
A tail-truncation budget sweep reveals a sharp performance jump at ${\sim}$512 tokens; this threshold coincides with the globals module dump (${\sim}$384 tokens), beyond which structured \texttt{[Line~X]} variable values appear (\S\ref{sec:trace_length}).

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Complete traces are strictly dominated by compact exception events}: across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}). Training dynamics directly show the mechanism: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).

\item \textbf{SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns beyond format matching}: a regex exploiting format markers matches the exception ceiling (99.33\%), but marker removal collapses it to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) confirms the learned signal generalizes (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

\item \textbf{A two-tier signal hierarchy with a practical trace selection strategy}: Tier~1 (exceptions, assertions; ${\geq}$98.53\%) dominates Tier~2 (loop compression; 77--86\%) by 12+pp with non-overlapping CIs across all four models. A sharp performance transition at ${\sim}$512 tail tokens yields a practical fallback: exception events first, tail-truncated state otherwise (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, \S\ref{sec:trace_length}).

\item \textbf{Controlled decomposition of the full-trace degradation}: gradient masking on \texttt{exception\_only} ($-$0.84pp under 99.8\% mask) limits gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\% of the 18pp gap; content quality (diagnostic signal density at inference) is the dominant factor at ${\geq}$95\%. A complementary label-only ablation on the Qwen family yields a directionally consistent but confounded upper bound (${\leq}$26\%) (\S\ref{sec:density}).
\end{enumerate}

None decompose which trace components contribute to \emph{classification} accuracy.

\paragraph{Code Verdict and Patch Classification.}
TRACED \citep{ding2024traced} showed execution-aware pretraining improves vulnerability detection; CC2Vec \citep{hoang2020cc2vec}, LLM4PatchCorrect \citep{zhou2024llm4patch}, and APPT \citep{appt2024} developed representation learning of code changes.
Verdict prediction is an instance of the test oracle problem \citep{barr2015oracle}; none isolate individual trace components.

\paragraph{Fault Localization and Trace Selection.}
SBFL \citep{abreu2007accuracy,jones2002visualization,wong2014dstar} and LLM-based FL \citep{kang2024autofl,qin2024agentfl} share our insight that anomalous execution events carry the strongest diagnostic signal.
TraceCoder \citep{huang2026tracecoder} and InspectCoder \citep{wang2025inspectcoder} use selective trace extraction; RepairAgent \citep{bouzenia2025repairagent}, Agentless \citep{xia2024agentless}, SWE-agent \citep{yang2024sweagent}, and OpenHands \citep{wang2025openhands} incorporate execution feedback in repair workflows \citep{jimenez2024swebench}, yet which trace components carry verdict signals most efficiently remains unstudied.
Prompt compression \citep{jiang2023llmlingua,li2023selectivecontext} showed pruning low-information tokens preserves accuracy; our decomposition quantifies \emph{why}.

\paragraph{Calibration, Data Selection, and Defect Prediction.}
Neural network calibration \citep{guo2017calibration}, extended to LLMs \citep{kadavath2022language,geng2024calibration,spiess2025calibration}, studies confidence-correctness alignment; our ECE ${<}$ 0.005 suggests compact inputs improve calibration.
The Information Bottleneck \citep{tishby2000information}, feature selection theory \citep{guyon2003introduction}, and LIMA \citep{zhou2023lima} predict that compressing task-irrelevant information improves learning; data pruning \citep{paul2021deep,sorscher2022beyond} and curriculum learning \citep{bengio2009curriculum} confirm this empirically, consistent with our finding that compact exceptions converge rapidly while verbose traces oscillate.

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结

### 4.1 目标

### 4.3 禁忌

This approach aligns with recent *CL precedent: CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval} uses execution prediction to probe code reasoning, and NExT \citep{ni2024next} uses trace-augmented chain-of-thought for program repair.

The central result: complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% across all models and seeds (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
A simple regex baseline (B5) that exploits the \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} format marker matches this ceiling at 99.33\%; even a trivial pattern suffices, so the interesting question is not why exceptions help but \emph{why complete traces hurt}.
Marker removal collapses B5 to 28.49\% while SFT retains 97.65\% ($-$2.01pp); bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) confirms that SFT acquires language-level diagnostic patterns beyond format matching (\S\ref{sec:nomarker}).

A controlled gradient masking ablation limits gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\% of the degradation; content quality---diagnostic signal density at inference, the mechanism underlying what is intuitively termed ``information overload''---accounts for ${\geq}$95\% (\S\ref{sec:density}).
Training dynamics confirm this: \texttt{exception\_only} converges within 50 steps, while \texttt{full\_trace} oscillates between 82--89\% without stable convergence (\S\ref{sec:ablation}, Appendix~\ref{sec:training_dynamics}).
A tail-truncation budget sweep reveals a sharp performance jump at ${\sim}$512 tokens; this threshold coincides with the globals module dump (${\sim}$384 tokens), beyond which structured \texttt{[Line~X]} variable values appear (\S\ref{sec:trace_length}).

\item \textbf{Complete traces are strictly dominated by compact exception events}: across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\% (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
